definition_en: a person who studies or works in science
core_image: 一位研究者俯身显微镜前，把刚看到的细节写进记录本
scene: 一位科学家在显微镜前记录观察结果。A scientist recorded her observations at the microscope.
sceneCN: 这里 scientist 是「科学家」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一位科学家在显微镜前记录观察结果。

senses.title: An expert in science
senses.definition: a person with expert knowledge of a science
senses.definitionCN: 拥有某门科学专业知识的人
senses.example: The scientist studied the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这位科学家研究了土壤。
senses.why: The core sense is a trained expert in a science.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是受过训练的科学专家。

senses.title: A researcher
senses.definition: a person who does scientific research
senses.definitionCN: 从事科学研究的人员
senses.example: Scientists warn about the risk.
senses.exampleCN: 科研人员警告这种风险。
senses.why: The role also covers people whose main work is research.
senses.whyCN: 这一称谓也涵盖以研究为主要工作的人。

intro.en: Scientist is science plus ist, a word coined in the 19th century.
intro.cn: scientist 由 science 加 ist 构成，是 19 世纪新造的词。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识。

items.en: Science narrowed to mean the study of nature.
items.cn: science 缩小为对自然的研究。

items.en: The word scientist was coined for people who study nature.
items.cn: scientist 一词被创造出来，指研究自然的人。

items.en: Scientist spread to every field of research.
items.cn: scientist 扩展到各个研究领域。

items.en: Scientist now means any trained researcher in science.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scientist 指任何受过训练的科研人员。

note.en: Scientist is compared with related words and with names for researchers.
note.cn: 把 scientist 与相关词以及表示研究者的名称作比较。

entries.definition: a person who studies a subject carefully

normalIntro.en: Scientist is science plus ist, the person who does the science.
normalIntro.cn: scientist 是 science 加 ist，即从事科学的人。

normal.en: Science is the field and scientist is the person.
normal.cn: science 是领域，scientist 是人。

normal.en: A computer scientist works with computing.
normal.cn: 计算机科学家研究计算。

normal.en: A social scientist studies people.
normal.cn: 社会科学家研究人。

normal.en: The ist ending often marks a person.
normal.cn: ist 结尾常表示人。

normal.en: Scientists test ideas before accepting them.
normal.cn: 科学家在接受想法前先检验它。

abstract.en: The word was invented when science became a profession.
abstract.cn: 当科学成为职业时，这个词被创造出来。

abstract.en: A scientist is defined by method, not by a single subject.
abstract.cn: 科学家的定义在于方法，而不限于单一学科。

abstract.en: The ist suffix turns a body of knowledge into a role.
abstract.cn: ist 后缀把知识体系变成一种角色。

examples.en: She became a scientist at twenty-five.
examples.cn: 她二十五岁时成为科学家。

examples.en: The scientists published their findings.
examples.cn: 科学家们发表了研究结果。

examples.en: A young scientist led the project.
examples.cn: 一位年轻科学家领导了这个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: science 是「科学」，ist 表示「从事……的人」，scientist 就是从事科学研究的人。

root: 由 science（科学）加表人后缀 ist 构成，19 世纪开始广泛使用。

sensesIntro.en: Scientist means an expert in a science or a person who does scientific research.
sensesIntro.cn: scientist 意为某门科学的专家，或从事科学研究的人。

core.en: A person whose work is producing scientific knowledge.
core.cn: 以产出科学知识为工作的人。

branches.en: A trained expert in one science.
branches.cn: 某门科学中受过训练的专家。

branches.en: A person whose daily work is research.
branches.cn: 以研究为日常工作的人。

branches.en: Expertise and research usually go together.
branches.cn: 专业知识与研究通常相伴。

branches.en: Both senses describe a scientific worker.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述科学工作者。

branches.en: The role can be in a lab, a field, or a classroom.
branches.cn: 这一角色可以出现在实验室、田野或课堂。

intro.en: Scientist belongs to the science family of people and methods.
intro.cn: scientist 属于由人物与方法词汇构成的 science 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scientia, knowledge, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scientia（知识）是远源。

items.exampleCN: 科学家提出了一个问题。
社会科学家研究了人群。

items.example: The computer scientist fixed the code.
items.exampleCN: 计算机科学家修复了代码。

definition_zh: 范围；机会；观察仪器；仔细查看
definition_en: the range something covers, the chance to do something, a viewing instrument, or to examine something carefully
core_image: 地图上用铅笔圈出的区域，边界线清楚地把范围标出来
scene: 这项研究的范围只包括本地居民。The scope of the study covers only local residents.
sceneCN: 这里 scope 是「范围」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这项研究的范围只包括本地居民。

senses.title: Range of coverage
senses.definition: the range of subjects or things something deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所涉及的主题或事物的范围
senses.example: The question is beyond the scope of this book.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题超出了本书的范围。
senses.why: The central sense is the boundary of what is included.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是所涵盖内容的边界。

senses.title: Chance to act
senses.definition: the opportunity or freedom to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的机会或自由空间
senses.example: There is scope for improvement.
senses.why: A range of action becomes a chance within that range.
senses.whyCN: 行动范围变成范围内的机会。

senses.title: A viewing instrument
senses.definition: a device for looking at something, often in compounds
senses.definitionCN: 用于观察某物的装置，常作构词成分
senses.example: The doctor used a scope to see inside.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用内窥镜查看内部。
senses.why: The Greek root meant a watcher, so instruments of sight took the word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为观看者，因此观察仪器用了这个词。

senses.title: To examine carefully
senses.definition: to look over something to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 查看某物以了解它
senses.example: They scoped out the new office.
senses.exampleCN: 他们仔细察看了新办公室。
senses.why: The noun of range becomes a verb of surveying.
senses.whyCN: 表示范围的名词转为勘察的动词。

intro.en: Scope comes from Greek skopos, a watcher or target, through Italian scopo.
intro.cn: scope 源自希腊语 skopos（观看者、目标），经意大利语 scopo 进入英语。

items.en: Skopos meant a watcher or a mark to aim at.
items.cn: skopos 意为观看者或瞄准的目标。

items.en: Scopo meant aim or purpose.
items.cn: scopo 意为目标或目的。

items.en: Scope entered English meaning purpose or aim.
items.cn: scope 进入英语时意为目的或目标。

items.en: Scope came to mean the range of a subject.
items.cn: scope 开始表示主题的范围。

items.en: Scope also names viewing instruments and the act of surveying.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scope 还指观察仪器与勘察行为。

note.en: Scope is compared with similar-looking words and with words for range and room.
note.cn: 把 scope 与形近词以及表示范围和余地的词作比较。

entries.definition: a deep spoon, or a news story
a surface that rises or falls
the limits between which something varies
the size or degree of something

normalIntro.en: Scope is the range you can see or reach, and also the instrument that helps you see.
normalIntro.cn: scope 是你能看到或触及的范围，也是帮助观看的仪器。

normal.en: The scope of a study is what it covers.
normal.cn: 研究范围就是它涵盖的内容。

normal.en: Scope for improvement means room to do better.
normal.cn: scope for improvement 意为改进余地。

normal.en: Telescope and microscope both end in scope.
normal.cn: telescope 与 microscope 都以 scope 结尾。

normal.en: To scope out a place is to look it over.
normal.cn: scope out 一个地方就是察看它。

normal.en: Beyond the scope means outside the limits.
normal.cn: beyond the scope 意为超出范围。

abstract.en: The Greek root joins watching with aiming.
abstract.cn: 希腊词根把观看与瞄准连在一起。

abstract.en: What you can see defines what you can do.
abstract.cn: 能看到的范围界定了能行动的范围。

abstract.en: Instruments of sight carry the name of the act of seeing.
abstract.cn: 观察仪器沿用「看」这一动作的名称。

examples.en: The question is beyond the scope of this book.
examples.cn: 这个问题超出了本书的范围。

examples.en: There is scope for improvement.
They scoped out the new office.
examples.cn: 他们仔细察看了新办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: scope 源自希腊语 skopos（观看者、目标），所以 telescope 是「看远处」，microscope 是「看微小」，scope 本身指「观察范围」。

root: 源自希腊语 skopos（观看者、目标），核心义「目光所及与目标所在的范围」。

sensesIntro.en: Scope means the range covered, the chance to act, a viewing instrument, or the act of examining.
sensesIntro.cn: scope 意为涵盖范围、行动余地、观察仪器，或仔细查看。

core.en: The field that sight or action can reach.
core.cn: 目光或行动能够到达的领域。

branches.en: The limits of what a subject includes.
branches.cn: 某个主题所包含的界限。

branches.en: The freedom to do something within limits.
branches.cn: 在界限内做某事的自由。

branches.en: A device that extends sight.
The act of looking something over.
A clear range creates a real chance to act.
branches.cn: 清晰的范围创造出真实的行动机会。

intro.en: Scope forms names for instruments of sight and for surveying.
intro.cn: scope 构成表示观察仪器与勘察的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek skopos passed through Italian scopo into English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 skopos 经意大利语 scopo 进入英语。

items.example: Each team scopes its own area.
items.exampleCN: 每个小组察看自己的区域。

items.meaning: surveyed, or fitted with a scope
items.example: The scoped rifle lay on the table.
items.exampleCN: 带瞄准镜的步枪放在桌上。

items.example: Scoping the project took a week.
items.exampleCN: 界定项目范围花了一周。

items.meaning: an instrument for seeing small things
items.example: The cells are visible under a microscope.

items.meaning: an instrument for seeing distant things
items.example: They watched the stars with a telescope.
items.exampleCN: 他们用望远镜观察星星。

items.meaning: a tube for seeing above or around
a tube for seeing inside the body
to examine a place or plan
items.example: We scoped out the route first.

definition_zh: 得分；比分；成绩；二十；配乐
definition_en: the number of points in a game, a mark or result, a group of twenty, or music for a film or play
core_image: 球场大屏幕上的比分牌翻到最后一分，观众全部站起来
scene: 终场哨响，球迷们抬头看大屏幕。The final score was three to two.
sceneCN: 这里 score 是「得分；比分」（第 1 个义项）；句意：最终比分是三比二。

senses.title: Points in a game
senses.definition: the number of points won in a game or competition
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或竞赛中赢得的分数
senses.example: He scored twice in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 他在下半场进了两个球。
senses.why: The central modern sense is points in a contest.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是竞赛中的得分。

senses.title: A mark or result
senses.definition: the result of a test or assessment
senses.definitionCN: 考试或评估的结果
senses.example: Her test score improved.
senses.why: The game sense extends to any measured result.
senses.whyCN: 比赛义延伸到任何被测量的结果。

senses.title: A group of twenty
senses.definition: a set or group of twenty
senses.definitionCN: 由二十个组成的一组
senses.example: A score of people waited outside.
senses.why: A tally mark for twenty gave the word this counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 表示二十的刻痕计数赋予该词这一数量义。

senses.title: Music for a film
senses.definition: the music written for a film, play, or show
senses.definitionCN: 为电影、戏剧或演出创作的音乐
senses.example: The film score was written in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的配乐一个月就写好了。
senses.why: A written score is a set of musical marks, like a tally.
senses.whyCN: 乐谱是一组记下的符号，如同刻痕计数。

intro.en: Score comes from Old Norse skor, a notch or tally mark.
intro.cn: score 源自古诺尔斯语 skor（刻痕、计数刻线）。

items.en: Skor meant a notch cut into wood.
items.cn: skor 意为刻在木头上的刻痕。

items.en: Score named a tally kept by notches.
items.cn: score 指用刻痕记录的账目。

items.en: A score of twenty became a standard count.
items.cn: 以二十为一组的计数成为标准。

items.en: Score named the points kept in games.
items.cn: score 开始指比赛中记录的分数。

items.en: Score also means written music for a film or play.
items.cn: 现代英语中 score 还指电影或戏剧的配乐。

note.en: Score is compared with similar-looking words and with words for points and marks.
note.cn: 把 score 与形近词以及表示分数与成绩的词作比较。

entries.definition: a unit of score in a game

normalIntro.en: Score began as a notch used for counting and now names points and music.
normalIntro.cn: score 起初是计数用的刻痕，现在指得分与配乐。

normal.en: The final score decides the winner.
normal.cn: 最终比分决定胜者。

normal.en: A test score measures a result.
normal.cn: 考试分数衡量结果。

normal.en: A score of people means twenty people.
normal.cn: a score of people 指二十个人。

normal.en: A film score is its music.
normal.cn: film score 是电影配乐。

normal.en: To score is to win a point.
normal.cn: to score 就是得分。

abstract.en: Counting by notches connects twenty, games, and music.
abstract.cn: 刻痕计数把二十、比赛与音乐连接起来。

abstract.en: A score is a record of what has been counted.
abstract.cn: score 是被计数内容的记录。

abstract.en: Music on a page is also a kind of tally of sounds.
abstract.cn: 纸上的音乐也是一种声音的记录。

examples.en: The final score was three to two.
Her test score improved.
The film score won an award.
examples.cn: 这部电影的配乐获了奖。

dict_mnemonic.text: score 源自古诺尔斯语 skor（刻痕），古人用刻痕计数，二十为一组，所以 score 又有「二十」义；比赛记分也来自刻痕计数。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 skor（刻痕、计数刻线），核心义「用刻痕记录的数量与得分」。

sensesIntro.en: Score means points in a game, a test result, a group of twenty, or music for a film.
sensesIntro.cn: score 意为比赛得分、考试成绩、二十，或电影配乐。

core.en: A record of counting, from notches to points.
core.cn: 从刻痕到得分的计数记录。

branches.en: Points recorded in a contest.
A measured result on a test.
A counted group of twenty.
Written music for a production.
Games and tests both turn performance into numbers.
branches.cn: 比赛与考试都把表现转化为数字。

intro.en: Score forms words for scoring, players, and music marks.
intro.cn: score 构成表示记分、得分者与音乐记号的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Old Norse skor is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古诺尔斯语 skor 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: Scores rose after the new rules.
items.exampleCN: 新规则实施后分数上升。

items.example: Scoring is easy in this game.

items.meaning: to emphasize or draw a line under

items.exampleCN: 这部电影配乐萦绕人心。

definition_zh: 抓；挠；划痕；从零开始；临时凑的
definition_en: to rub the skin with something sharp, a mark made by scratching, or something started or gathered from nothing
core_image: 猫伸出爪子，在沙发边缘留下几道细细的划痕
scene: 猫在沙发边缘抓了几下。The cat scratched the edge of the sofa.
sceneCN: 这里 scratch 是「抓；挠」（第 1 个义项）；句意：猫在沙发边缘抓了几下。

senses.title: To rub with something sharp
senses.definition: to rub the skin with nails or a sharp object
senses.definitionCN: 用指甲或尖锐物摩擦皮肤
senses.example: He scratched his head in confusion.
senses.why: The core sense is a quick, sharp rubbing motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是快速而尖锐的摩擦动作。

senses.title: A mark from scratching
senses.definition: a thin mark made by something sharp
senses.definitionCN: 由尖锐物造成的细长痕迹
senses.example: The table has a deep scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上有一道很深的划痕。
senses.why: The action leaves a visible line.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作留下可见的线条。

senses.title: From the very beginning
senses.definition: starting with nothing prepared or existing
senses.definitionCN: 从没有任何准备或基础的状态开始
senses.example: She built the site from scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 她白手起家建起了这个网站。
senses.why: Starting from scratch means starting before any mark is made.
senses.whyCN: 从零开始就像在任何痕迹出现之前起步。

senses.title: Gathered in a hurry
senses.definition: made or gathered quickly from whatever is available
senses.definitionCN: 用现有条件匆忙组成或收集的
senses.example: They fielded a scratch team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们临时凑了一支队伍。
senses.why: A scratch group is put together without planning.
senses.whyCN: 临时拼凑的群体没有经过计划。

intro.en: Scratch comes from Middle English scracchen, probably imitating the sound of scratching.
intro.cn: scratch 源自中古英语 scracchen，可能模仿刮擦的声音。

items.en: Scracchen meant to scratch or claw.
items.cn: scracchen 意为抓或挠。

items.en: Scratch named a mark made on a surface.
items.cn: scratch 指留在表面上的痕迹。

items.en: From scratch meant starting at the beginning line.
items.cn: from scratch 意为从起点线开始。

items.en: A scratch team meant one gathered in a hurry.
items.cn: scratch team 指匆忙凑成的队伍。

items.en: Scratch covers clawing, marks, and starting from zero.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scratch 涵盖抓挠、划痕与从零开始。

note.en: Scratch is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for scraping and clawing.
note.cn: 把 scratch 与形近词以及表示刮擦和抓挠的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to rub a hard edge over a surface
to make a high harsh sound
to mark a surface by rubbing

normalIntro.en: Scratch is a quick sharp action that leaves a mark.
normalIntro.cn: scratch 是留下痕迹的快速尖锐动作。

normal.en: A cat scratches with its claws.
normal.cn: 猫用爪子抓。

normal.en: Scratch your head when puzzled.
normal.cn: 困惑时挠挠头。

normal.en: Build from scratch means start with nothing.
normal.cn: from scratch 意为从零开始。

normal.en: Scratch the surface means barely begin.
normal.cn: scratch the surface 意为只触及表面。

normal.en: A scratchy sweater feels rough.
normal.cn: scratchy 的毛衣摸起来刺痒。

abstract.en: A scratch is a memory left on a surface.
abstract.cn: 划痕是留在表面上的记忆。

abstract.en: Starting from scratch means no marks exist yet.
abstract.cn: 从零开始意味着还没有任何痕迹。

abstract.en: The same word names the action, the mark, and the fresh start.
abstract.cn: 同一个词命名动作、痕迹与重新开始。

examples.en: He scratched his head in confusion.
The table has a deep scratch.
examples.cn: 桌上有一道很深的划痕。

examples.en: She built the site from scratch.
examples.cn: 她白手起家建起了这个网站。

dict_mnemonic.text: scratch 可能模仿刮擦声而来，核心是「用尖锐物划过表面」；from scratch 原指从起跑线开始，所以表示从零开始。

root: 源自中古英语 scracchen，拟声来源，核心义「用尖锐物快速划过表面」。

sensesIntro.en: Scratch means to claw the skin, a thin mark, a start from nothing, or a hurried gathering.
sensesIntro.cn: scratch 意为抓挠皮肤、细划痕、从零开始，或仓促拼凑。

core.en: A sharp mark made by a quick movement.
core.cn: 快速动作留下的尖锐痕迹。

branches.en: The act of clawing or rubbing.
The line left on a surface.
A beginning with nothing prepared.
A group formed in a hurry.
The action and its mark are one idea.
branches.cn: 动作与其痕迹是同一个概念。

intro.en: Scratch forms adjectives, notes, and common phrases.
intro.cn: scratch 构成形容词、便签词与常用短语。

latinIntro.en: Middle English scracchen is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 中古英语 scracchen 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.structure: English verb form and plural noun

items.example: He scratched his arm on a branch.

items.meaning: the act or sound of scratching
items.example: The scratching at the door frightened me.
items.exampleCN: 门口的抓挠声吓到了我。

items.example: Write the number on a scratchpad.

items.meaning: a card with a surface to scratch off

definition_en: to give a loud high cry, to shout very loudly, or such a cry
core_image: 过山车俯冲而下，乘客闭着眼张嘴尖叫
scene: 过山车俯冲时，她忍不住尖叫。She could not help screaming as the roller coaster dived.
sceneCN: 这里 scream 是「尖叫」（第 1 个义项）；句意：过山车俯冲时，她忍不住尖叫。

senses.title: A cry of fear or pain
senses.definition: to give a loud high cry because of fear, pain, or surprise
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、疼痛或惊讶而发出响亮高亢的叫声
senses.example: She screamed when she saw the spider.
senses.exampleCN: 她看到蜘蛛时尖叫起来。
senses.why: The core sense is a sudden high cry of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是情绪引发的突然高叫。

senses.title: To shout very loudly
senses.definition: to speak or call out at a very high volume
senses.definitionCN: 以极高音量说话或呼喊
senses.example: The crowd screamed with joy.
senses.why: The cry of feeling extends to any very loud call.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的叫喊延伸到任何高声呼喊。

senses.title: A high sharp sound
senses.definition: a loud high sound made by a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人或物发出的响亮高亢声音
senses.example: We heard a scream in the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里我们听到一声尖叫。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun for the sound itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为表示声音本身的名词。

intro.en: Scream comes from Middle English scremen, probably imitating the sound, and is related to Old Norse skræma, to scare.
intro.cn: scream 源自中古英语 scremen，可能是拟声词，并与古诺尔斯语 skræma（使害怕）有关。

items.en: Skræma meant to frighten or scare.
items.cn: skræma 意为使害怕或惊吓。

items.en: Scremen meant to cry out loudly.
items.cn: scremen 意为大声喊叫。

items.en: Scream named a sharp cry of fear or pain.
items.cn: scream 指恐惧或疼痛的尖锐叫声。

items.en: The word spread to loud sounds of joy and anger.
items.cn: 该词扩展到喜悦与愤怒的高声叫喊。

items.en: Scream also names any high harsh sound.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scream 还指任何高而刺耳的声音。

note.en: Scream is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for loud cries.
note.cn: 把 scream 与形近词以及表示高声叫喊的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a small river, or a flow
to give a high sharp cry

normalIntro.en: Scream is the loud high cry of fear, pain, or excitement.
normalIntro.cn: scream 是恐惧、疼痛或兴奋时的高声尖叫。

normal.en: A scream is high and sharp.
normal.cn: 尖叫又高又尖。

normal.en: Scream for help when in danger.
normal.cn: 遇险时大声呼救。

normal.en: Scream at someone shows anger.
normal.cn: 对某人大喊表示愤怒。

normal.en: Screaming can be joy as well as fear.
normal.cn: 尖叫既可以表示恐惧，也可以表示喜悦。

normal.en: A scream of laughter is a burst of laughter.
normal.cn: a scream of laughter 指一阵大笑。

abstract.en: Sound carries feeling more directly than words.
abstract.cn: 声音比词语更直接地承载情绪。

abstract.en: The same cry serves fear, pain, and excitement.
abstract.cn: 同一种叫喊服务于恐惧、疼痛与兴奋。

abstract.en: Scream turns a sudden feeling into a public sound.
abstract.cn: 尖叫把突然的情绪变成公开的声音。

examples.cn: 她看到蜘蛛时尖叫起来。

examples.en: The crowd screamed with joy.

dict_mnemonic.text: scream 可能是模仿尖叫声造出的词，与表示「使害怕」的古诺尔斯语词有关；核心是「高而尖的叫声」。

root: 源自中古英语 scremen，拟声来源，并与古诺尔斯语 skræma（使害怕）相关，核心义「高而尖的叫声」。

sensesIntro.en: Scream means to cry out in fear or pain, to shout very loudly, or such a high sound.
sensesIntro.cn: scream 意为因恐惧或疼痛尖叫、大声喊叫，或这种高亢声音。

core.en: A high sound forced out by strong feeling.
core.cn: 被强烈情绪逼出的高亢声音。

branches.en: A sudden cry of fear or pain.

branches.en: A very loud shout of any feeling.
branches.cn: 任何情绪下的高声喊叫。

branches.en: The sound itself as a noun.

branches.cn: 动作与声音共用一个名称。

intro.en: Scream forms adjectives, nouns, and common phrases about loud cries.
intro.cn: scream 构成表示高声叫喊的形容词、名词与常用短语。

items.meaning: to cry loudly, or such a cry
items.example: Do not scream in the library.

items.meaning: a person or thing that screams

items.exampleCN: 这个过山车真让人尖叫。

items.meaning: several people or things that scream
to cry out to be rescued

definition_zh: 屏幕；银幕；屏风；筛查；遮挡
definition_en: a flat surface showing images, the cinema, a protective panel, to examine for suitability, or to hide something
core_image: 黑暗的客厅里，电视屏幕忽然亮起，映出一张脸
scene: 手机屏幕在黑暗的房间里亮了起来。The phone screen lit up in the dark room.
sceneCN: 这里 screen 是「屏幕」（第 1 个义项）；句意：手机屏幕在黑暗的房间里亮了起来。

senses.title: A display surface
senses.definition: a flat surface on which images or words are shown
senses.definitionCN: 显示图像或文字的平面
senses.example: The phone screen lit up in the dark room.
senses.exampleCN: 手机屏幕在黑暗的房间里亮了起来。
senses.why: The central modern sense is the surface that shows images.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是显示图像的表面。

senses.title: The cinema
senses.definition: the large screen in a cinema, or film as a medium
senses.definitionCN: 电影院的大银幕，或作为媒介的电影
senses.example: The film was shown on a big screen.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影在大银幕上放映。
senses.why: The display surface stands for the medium shown on it.
senses.whyCN: 显示表面代指在其上呈现的媒介。

senses.title: A protective panel
senses.definition: a piece of material used to block view, wind, or light
senses.definitionCN: 用于挡视线、挡风或遮光的材料
senses.example: A folding screen divided the room.
senses.why: The oldest sense is something that stands in front.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是挡在前面的东西。

senses.title: To examine for suitability
senses.definition: to check people or things to decide if they are suitable or safe
senses.definitionCN: 检查人或物以判断是否合适或安全
senses.example: Doctors screen patients for the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 医生为病人筛查这种疾病。
senses.why: A screen separates what passes from what does not.
senses.whyCN: 筛子把通过者与不通过者分开。

senses.title: To hide from view
senses.definition: to protect or hide something behind a screen
senses.definitionCN: 把某物挡在遮蔽物后面以保护或隐藏
senses.example: Clouds screened the sun.
senses.why: The panel sense becomes the act of blocking.
senses.whyCN: 遮蔽物义转变为遮挡动作。

intro.en: Screen comes from Old French escren, a screen or shield, probably from Middle Dutch scherm.
intro.cn: screen 源自古法语 escren（屏风、遮挡物），可能来自中古荷兰语 scherm。

items.en: Scherm meant a shield or protection.
items.cn: scherm 意为盾牌或保护物。

items.en: Escren meant a screen against heat or view.
items.cn: escren 意为挡热或挡视线的屏风。

items.en: Screen named a panel that blocks view or wind.
items.cn: screen 指遮挡视线或风的屏风。

items.en: Screen came to mean a surface for showing images.
items.cn: screen 开始指显示图像的表面。

items.en: Screen also means to examine or to hide.
items.cn: 现代英语中 screen 还表示筛查或遮挡。

note.en: Screen is compared with similar-looking words and with words for displays and filters.
note.cn: 把 screen 与形近词以及表示显示和筛选的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flow of water or data
a screen used with a computer

normalIntro.en: Screen began as a shield and now names displays and filtering.
normalIntro.cn: screen 起初是遮挡物，现在指显示屏与筛选。

normal.en: A screen shows images.
normal.cn: 屏幕显示图像。

normal.en: The big screen means the cinema.
normal.cn: the big screen 指电影院。

normal.en: A screen can block wind or light.
normal.cn: 屏风可以挡风或遮光。

normal.en: To screen patients is to test them.
normal.cn: 筛查病人就是检测他们。

normal.en: Sunscreen screens the skin from the sun.
normal.cn: 防晒霜为皮肤遮挡阳光。

abstract.en: A screen both shows and hides.
abstract.cn: 屏幕既展示，也遮蔽。

abstract.en: The idea of a barrier links panels, displays, and filters.
abstract.cn: 屏障概念连接了屏风、显示屏与筛子。

abstract.en: To screen is to decide what may pass.
abstract.cn: 筛查就是决定什么可以通过。

examples.en: The film was shown on a big screen.
examples.cn: 这部电影在大银幕上放映。

examples.en: Doctors screen patients for the disease.
examples.cn: 医生为病人筛查这种疾病。

examples.en: Clouds screened the sun.

dict_mnemonic.text: screen 原指挡风的屏风，后来指隔开视线的平面，再指电视与手机屏幕；「筛查」义来自「用筛子隔开」。

root: 源自古法语 escren（屏风、遮挡物），来自中古荷兰语 scherm，核心义「挡在面前的一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Screen means a display surface, the cinema, a protective panel, to examine, or to hide something.

core.en: A surface that shows, hides, or separates.

branches.en: A surface that shows images.
The cinema as a medium.

intro.en: Screen forms words for films, devices, and protection.

items.example: The windows were screened from view.

items.meaning: a test or a film showing
an image shown on an idle screen

items.example: The story returned to the big screen.

definition_en: a metal pin with a spiral ridge, to turn it into place, a spiral form, or to ruin something in informal use
core_image: 螺丝刀把一枚螺丝一点点拧进木板，木屑从螺纹间挤出
scene: 他用螺丝刀把螺丝拧进木板。He drove the screw into the wood with a screwdriver.
sceneCN: 这里 screw 是「螺丝」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用螺丝刀把螺丝拧进木板。

senses.title: A spiral fastener
senses.definition: a metal pin with a spiral ridge, used to join things
senses.definitionCN: 带螺旋纹、用于连接物体的金属钉
senses.example: Tighten the screw with a screwdriver.
senses.why: The core sense is the fastening object.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是紧固物件。

senses.title: To turn into place
senses.definition: to turn a screw or lid so that it goes in or comes off
senses.definitionCN: 旋转螺丝或盖子使其进入或脱开
senses.example: He screwed the lid onto the jar.
senses.why: The object's use becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 物件的用途变成动作。

senses.title: A spiral form
senses.definition: a shape that winds around like a screw thread
senses.definitionCN: 像螺纹一样盘绕的形状
senses.example: The staircase winds in a screw.
senses.why: The shape that lets a screw grip becomes a general form.
senses.whyCN: 让螺丝咬合的形态成为一种普遍形状。

senses.title: To ruin or cheat
senses.definition: to ruin something, or to cheat someone, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中搞砸某事或欺骗某人
senses.example: He screwed the deal by arriving late.
senses.exampleCN: 他因迟到把交易搞砸了。
senses.why: A twisted thread becomes an image of things going wrong.
senses.whyCN: 扭曲的螺纹成为事情出错的意象。

intro.en: Screw probably comes from Old French escroue, a nut or screw, perhaps from Latin scrofa, a sow.
intro.cn: screw 可能源自古法语 escroue（螺母、螺丝），也许来自拉丁语 scrofa（母猪）。

items.en: Scrofa meant a sow, perhaps because of the curled shape.
items.cn: scrofa 意为母猪，可能因卷曲形状而得名。

items.en: Escroue meant a nut or a screw.
items.cn: escroue 意为螺母或螺丝。

items.en: Screw named a spiral fastening device.
items.cn: screw 指螺旋紧固装置。

items.en: Screw also meant to turn something into place.
items.cn: screw 也开始表示旋转固定。

items.en: Screw has informal senses of ruining or cheating.
items.cn: 现代英语中 screw 有搞砸或欺骗的非正式义。

note.en: Screw is compared with similar-looking words and with words for fasteners and turning.
note.cn: 把 screw 与形近词以及表示紧固件和旋转的词作比较。

to move something in a circle

normalIntro.en: A screw is a spiral fastener, and to screw is to turn it.

normal.en: A screwdriver turns a screw.
normal.cn: 螺丝刀转动螺丝。

normal.en: Screw the lid on tightly.
normal.cn: 把盖子拧紧。

normal.en: Unscrew means turn the other way.
normal.cn: unscrew 意为反方向拧开。

abstract.en: The same turning motion can fix or destroy.

abstract.en: The tool and its shape share one short word.

examples.en: Tighten the screw with a screwdriver.
He screwed the lid onto the jar.
She screwed up the plan.

dict_mnemonic.text: screw 可能经古法语 escroue 来自拉丁语 scrofa（母猪），因螺旋形似猪尾而得名；核心是「螺旋纹的紧固件」。

root: 可能经古法语 escroue 源自拉丁语 scrofa（母猪），核心义「带螺旋纹、可旋转固定的物件」。

sensesIntro.en: Screw means a spiral fastener, to turn it, a spiral form, or to ruin something informally.
sensesIntro.cn: screw 意为螺丝、拧紧、螺旋，或非正式地搞砸。

core.en: A spiral that grips as it turns.
core.cn: 旋转时产生咬合的螺旋。

branches.en: The metal fastener itself.
The act of turning it into place.
branches.cn: 把它旋转固定到位的动作。

branches.en: The spiral shape of the thread.
A plan twisted into failure.
The object and its use are inseparable.

intro.en: Screw forms tools, adjectives, and common phrasal verbs.
intro.cn: screw 构成工具、形容词与常用短语动词。

items.meaning: to ruin or make a mistake

definition_en: the written text of a film or play, a system of writing, a person's handwriting, or a set of computer instructions
core_image: 桌上摊开一份剧本，页边写满演员用铅笔做的批注
scene: 演员们在开拍前围读剧本。The actors read the script together before filming.
sceneCN: 这里 script 是「剧本」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演员们在开拍前围读剧本。

senses.title: A text for a film or play
senses.definition: the written words and directions for a film, play, or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 电影、戏剧或广播的台词与说明文字
senses.example: The script needs another rewrite.
senses.exampleCN: 这个剧本还需要再改一稿。
senses.why: The central modern sense is the text actors follow.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是演员照读的文本。

senses.title: A system of writing
senses.definition: a set of written symbols used by a language
senses.definitionCN: 某种语言使用的一套书写符号
senses.example: These languages use different scripts.
senses.exampleCN: 这些语言使用不同的文字体系。
senses.why: Any written text is a script, so a whole writing system took the name.
senses.whyCN: 任何写下的文本都是 script，于是整套书写系统也用了这个词。

senses.title: A person's handwriting
senses.definition: the way a particular person writes by hand
senses.definitionCN: 某个人手写时的字体样式
senses.example: His script is small and neat.
senses.why: Handwriting is the most personal kind of written text.
senses.whyCN: 笔迹是最个人化的书写文本。

senses.title: Computer instructions
senses.definition: a set of instructions that a computer follows
senses.definitionCN: 计算机按顺序执行的一组指令
senses.example: The script runs every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个脚本每天早上运行。
senses.why: A script is a text a machine reads and follows.
senses.whyCN: 脚本是机器阅读并执行的文本。

items.en: Scribere meant to write.
items.cn: scribere 意为写。

items.en: Scriptum meant something written.
items.cn: scriptum 意为写下的东西。

items.en: Script meant a written document.
items.cn: script 意为书面文件。

items.en: Script came to mean the text of a play.

items.en: Script also names writing systems and computer code.

note.en: Script is compared with similar-looking words and with words for written texts.

normalIntro.en: Script is anything written, from a play to computer code.
normalIntro.cn: script 是任何写下来的东西，从剧本到计算机代码。

normal.en: Actors read a script.

normal.en: Different languages use different scripts.
normal.cn: 不同语言使用不同文字体系。

normal.en: Neat script means neat handwriting.

normal.en: A computer script runs instructions.

normal.en: A scriptwriter writes scripts.

abstract.en: A play, a writing system, and code are all texts to be read.
abstract.cn: 戏剧、文字体系与代码都是供阅读的文本。

abstract.en: Script links human writing with machine reading.

examples.en: The script needs another rewrite.
examples.cn: 这个剧本还需要再改一稿。

examples.en: These languages use different scripts.
examples.cn: 这些语言使用不同的文字体系。

examples.en: The script runs every morning.
examples.cn: 这个脚本每天早上运行。

branches.cn: 两者都是供阅读的文本。

intro.en: Script forms words for writers, documents, and notes.
intro.cn: script 构成表示作者、文件与附言的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin scribere and scriptum are the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scribere 与 scriptum 是词源。

items.example: The desk is covered with scripts.

items.exampleCN: 这个节目感觉太照本宣科了。
编写脚本能节省数小时工作。

items.example: The manuscript is in the archive.

items.meaning: a note added after a letter
a character set below the line

definition_en: the large body of salt water covering much of the earth, a large amount, or the state of the waves
core_image: 蓝色海面一直延伸到天际，白色浪花一层层涌上沙滩
scene: 孩子们光着脚跑向海边。The children ran barefoot toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sea 是「海；海洋」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们光着脚跑向海边。

senses.title: The salt water body
senses.definition: the large body of salt water that covers much of the earth
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: The sea was calm at dawn.
senses.why: The central sense is the great body of salt water.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是巨大的咸水体。

senses.title: A huge amount
senses.definition: a very large number or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物数量极多的一大片
senses.example: A sea of people filled the square.
senses.why: A boundless expanse becomes an image of great quantity.
senses.whyCN: 无边无际的景象成为数量的比喻。

senses.title: The state of the waves
senses.definition: the condition of the waves on the sea
senses.definitionCN: 海面上波浪的状况
senses.example: The ship sailed into rough seas.
senses.exampleCN: 船驶入了波涛汹涌的海面。
senses.why: The place sense narrows to the water's surface condition.
senses.whyCN: 场所义缩小为水面状况。

intro.en: Sea comes from Old English sæ, a word shared with other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: sea 源自古英语 sæ，与其他日耳曼语言同源。

items.en: Sæ meant the sea or a large lake.
items.cn: sæ 意为海或大湖。

items.en: See named the great body of salt water.
items.cn: see 指巨大的咸水体。

items.en: Sea appeared in many compounds for travel and trade.
items.cn: sea 大量出现在航海与贸易复合词中。

items.en: A sea of something became a common image of quantity.
items.cn: a sea of 成为表示数量的常见比喻。

items.en: Sea means the ocean, its surface, or a vast amount.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sea 指海洋、海面或大量。

note.en: Sea is compared with similar short words and with words for large waters.
note.cn: 把 sea 与形近短词以及表示大片水域的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sea animal, or a stamp
one of the great bodies of salt water
the clear liquid in seas and rivers

normalIntro.en: Sea is the salt water, its waves, and any vast expanse.
normalIntro.cn: sea 是咸水、海浪，也是任何广阔的景象。

normal.en: Sea and see sound the same.
normal.cn: sea 与 see 发音相同。

normal.en: By the sea means near the coast.
normal.cn: by the sea 意为在海边。

normal.en: Sea level is the height of the ocean surface.
normal.cn: sea level 是海平面高度。

normal.en: Seafood comes from the sea.
normal.cn: 海鲜来自海洋。

normal.en: A sea of faces means a huge crowd.
normal.cn: a sea of faces 指人山人海。

abstract.en: A boundless surface easily becomes a metaphor for quantity.
abstract.cn: 无边无际的表面很容易成为数量的比喻。

abstract.en: The same word names the water, its waves, and its scale.
abstract.cn: 同一个词命名水体、波浪与规模。

abstract.en: Sea connects geography with feeling.
abstract.cn: sea 把地理与情感连接起来。

examples.en: The sea was calm at dawn.
They live by the sea.
A sea of people filled the square.

dict_mnemonic.text: sea 是「海」，与 see 同音；seaside 是海滨，seafood 是海鲜，sea level 是海平面。

root: 源自古英语 sæ（海、大湖），核心义「覆盖大片地表的咸水体」。

sensesIntro.en: Sea means the salt water body, a vast amount, or the condition of the waves.
sensesIntro.cn: sea 意为海洋、大量，或海面波浪状况。

core.en: A vast body of salt water.
core.cn: 巨大的咸水体。

branches.en: The ocean itself.
A crowd or amount like an ocean.
branches.cn: 像海洋一样的数量或人群。

branches.en: The movement and mood of the water.
The vast body inspires images of scale.
branches.cn: 巨大的水体激发规模想象。

branches.en: Water and waves are one experience.
branches.cn: 海水与波浪是同一体验。

intro.en: Sea forms compounds for coast, travel, and food.
intro.cn: sea 构成表示海岸、航海与食物的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Old English sæ is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 sæ 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: We spent a week at the seaside.

items.exampleCN: 这个海港承担大量贸易。

items.meaning: a bird that lives near the sea
the average height of the sea
items.example: The town lies below sea level.

definition_en: a sea animal with flippers, a stamped mark, a closed fastening, or to close something tightly
core_image: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳，胡须上还挂着水珠
scene: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。A seal lay on the ice in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 seal 是「海豹」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。

senses.title: A sea animal
senses.definition: a sea animal with flippers that rests on land or ice
senses.definitionCN: 有鳍状肢、在陆地或冰上休息的海洋动物
senses.example: A seal swam beside the boat.
senses.why: One word comes from an old name for this animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的一个来源就是这种动物的古称。

senses.title: A stamped mark
senses.definition: a device or mark pressed onto a document to prove it is genuine
senses.definitionCN: 盖在文件上以证明其真实的器具或印记
senses.example: The letter bore the king's seal.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信上有国王的印章。
senses.why: A pressed mark closes and certifies a document.
senses.whyCN: 压印的标记封闭并证明文件。

senses.title: A closed fastening
senses.definition: something that closes an opening tightly
senses.definitionCN: 把开口紧密封闭的东西
senses.example: The seal on the jar was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子上的封口被打开了。
senses.why: The certified mark becomes a physical closure.
senses.whyCN: 认证标记变成物理封口。

senses.title: To close tightly
senses.definition: to close something so that air or liquid cannot pass
senses.definitionCN: 封闭某物使空气或液体无法通过
senses.example: She sealed the envelope with wax.
senses.why: The noun of closure becomes the action of closing.
senses.whyCN: 封闭物的名词义转为封闭动作。

intro.en: Seal is two words in one: Old English seolh, the animal, and Latin sigillum, a small stamp.
intro.cn: seal 是两个词合流：古英语 seolh（海豹）与拉丁语 sigillum（小图章）。

items.en: Seolh named the sea animal.
items.cn: seolh 指海豹这种海洋动物。

items.en: Sigillum meant a small picture or stamp.
items.cn: sigillum 意为小图像或印章。

items.en: Seel meant a stamp used on documents.
items.cn: seel 指用于文件的印章。

items.en: Seal named both the animal and the stamp.
items.cn: seal 同时指海豹与印章。

items.en: Seal also meant to close a document formally.
items.cn: seal 也开始表示正式封住文件。

items.en: Seal means to close tightly or to block an area.
items.cn: 现代英语中 seal 意为密封或封锁区域。

note.en: Seal is compared with similar short words and with words for stamps and closures.
note.cn: 把 seal 与形近短词以及表示印章和封闭的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small mark or device pressed on paper
a small seal, often in a ring

normalIntro.en: Seal is an animal and also a stamp that closes a document.
normalIntro.cn: seal 既是海豹，也是封住文件的印章。

normal.en: A seal lives in cold seas.
normal.cn: 海豹生活在寒冷海域。

normal.en: A wax seal closes a letter.
normal.cn: 蜡封印封住信件。

normal.en: Seal the envelope before posting.
normal.cn: 寄出前把信封封好。

normal.en: Police sealed off the street.
normal.cn: 警察封锁了街道。

normal.en: Seal and sea look alike.
normal.cn: seal 与 sea 形近。

abstract.en: Two unrelated words became one spelling.
abstract.cn: 两个无关的词变成了同一个拼写。

abstract.en: A stamp that proves a document also closes it.
abstract.cn: 证明文件的印章同时也封闭文件。

abstract.en: Closing and certifying share one gesture.
abstract.cn: 封闭与认证共享同一个动作。

examples.en: The envelope was sealed with wax.
Police sealed off the street.
A seal swam beside the boat.

dict_mnemonic.text: seal 有两个来源：古英语 seolh 指海豹，拉丁语 sigillum 指印章；「密封」义从盖印章封住文件发展而来。

root: 双源词：海豹义来自古英语 seolh；印章与密封义来自拉丁语 sigillum（小图章）。

sensesIntro.en: Seal means a sea animal, a stamped mark, a closure, or to close something tightly.
sensesIntro.cn: seal 意为海豹、印章、封口，或密封。

core.en: A mark or closure that makes something secure.
core.cn: 使某物安全可靠的印记或封闭。

branches.en: The animal of cold seas.
A mark that proves a document.
A physical closure on a container.
The action of closing tightly.
Stamping and sealing both finish a document.
branches.cn: 盖章与密封都完成文件处理。

intro.en: Seal forms words for closing materials and actions.
intro.cn: seal 构成表示密封材料与动作的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin sigillum is the source of the stamp sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sigillum 是印章义的来源。

items.meaning: an animal, a stamp, or to close

items.example: Sealing the jar keeps food fresh.
items.exampleCN: 密封罐子能让食物保鲜。

items.meaning: a substance or person that seals

items.exampleCN: 法院公开了密封的记录。

items.example: He wore a silver seal ring.
items.exampleCN: 他戴着一枚银印章戒指。

definition_en: to look carefully for something, to examine a place, or the act of looking
core_image: 手电筒的光柱在黑暗房间里来回移动，寻找丢失的钥匙
scene: 他们在黑暗的房间里寻找钥匙。They searched the dark room for the key.
sceneCN: 这里 search 是「搜索；寻找」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在黑暗的房间里寻找钥匙。

senses.title: To look for something
senses.definition: to look carefully for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 仔细寻找某物或某人
senses.example: She searched for her keys.
senses.why: The central sense is looking for something lost or wanted.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是寻找丢失或想要的东西。

senses.title: To examine a place
senses.definition: to examine a place or person thoroughly
senses.definitionCN: 彻底检查某个地方或某个人
senses.example: The police searched the house.
senses.why: Looking for something becomes a formal examination of a place.
senses.whyCN: 寻找某物变成对场所的正式检查。

senses.title: An act of looking
senses.definition: an attempt to find something
senses.definitionCN: 寻找某物的尝试
senses.example: The search took two hours.
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun for the whole effort.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为表示整个努力过程的名词。

intro.en: Search comes from Old French cerchier, from Latin circare, to go around.
intro.cn: search 源自古法语 cerchier，来自拉丁语 circare（绕行）。

items.en: Circare meant to go around or wander over.
items.cn: circare 意为绕行或走遍。

items.en: Cerchier meant to look through a place.
items.cn: cerchier 意为搜遍一个地方。

items.en: Serchen meant to examine or look for.
items.cn: serchen 意为检查或寻找。

items.en: Search named an official examination.
items.cn: search 指正式检查。

items.en: Search covers looking, examining, and online finding.
items.cn: 现代英语中 search 涵盖寻找、搜查与网络检索。

note.en: Search is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for seeking.
note.cn: 把 search 与形近词以及表示寻找的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a place where a bird rests
to try to find or obtain

normalIntro.en: Search is looking for something, and also the whole attempt.
normalIntro.cn: search 是寻找某物，也指整个寻找过程。

normal.en: Search for your keys.
normal.cn: 寻找你的钥匙。

normal.en: A search engine finds pages.
normal.cn: 搜索引擎查找网页。

normal.en: In search of means looking for.
normal.cn: in search of 意为寻找。

normal.en: Police search a house.
normal.cn: 警察搜查房屋。

normal.en: Research adds re to search.
normal.cn: research 是在 search 前加 re。

abstract.en: Search began as going around a place.
abstract.cn: search 最初指绕遍一个地方。

abstract.en: Looking for an object and examining a place share one verb.
abstract.cn: 找东西与查地方共用一个动词。

abstract.en: The noun turns a moment of looking into a process.
abstract.cn: 名词义把一次寻找变成一段过程。

examples.en: She searched for her keys.
The police searched the house.
The search took two hours.

dict_mnemonic.text: search 源自拉丁语 circare（绕行），原义是「走遍一个地方去找」，所以既指寻找，也指搜查。

root: 源自古法语 cerchier，来自拉丁语 circare（绕行），核心义「走遍某处寻找」。

sensesIntro.en: Search means to look for something, to examine a place, or the act of looking.
sensesIntro.cn: search 意为寻找某物、搜查某地，或搜寻行为。

core.en: Moving through a place to find something.
core.cn: 走遍某地以寻找某物。

branches.en: Looking for a lost or wanted thing.
branches.cn: 寻找丢失或想要的东西。

branches.en: Examining a place for evidence.
branches.cn: 为寻找证据而检查某地。

branches.en: The effort as a whole.
Both senses involve careful looking.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及仔细查看。

branches.en: The action and the effort share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与过程共用一个词。

intro.en: Search forms words for research, people, and tools.
intro.cn: search 构成表示研究、人物与工具的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin circare, to go around, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circare（绕行）是远源。

items.meaning: to look for, or an attempt to find

items.example: She gave him a searching look.

items.meaning: a service that finds web pages
items.example: The search engine returned many results.
items.exampleCN: 搜索引擎返回了许多结果。

items.example: A search party combed the woods.

definition_en: one of the four parts of the year, a particular period, or to add flavour to food
core_image: 同一棵树在四季里的四张照片，从新芽到积雪
scene: 秋天是苹果成熟的季节。Autumn is the season when apples ripen.
sceneCN: 这里 season 是「季节」（第 1 个义项）；句意：秋天是苹果成熟的季节。

senses.title: One of four parts of the year
senses.definition: one of the four main periods of the year marked by weather
senses.definitionCN: 一年中由天气划分的四个主要时期之一
senses.example: Winter is the coldest season.
senses.why: The central sense is a division of the year.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一年中的一个时段。

senses.title: A particular period
senses.definition: a period when an activity usually happens
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动通常发生的时期
senses.example: The hotel is busy in season.
senses.why: The yearly division narrows to a busy or usual time.
senses.whyCN: 年度划分缩小为繁忙或惯常时期。

senses.title: To add flavour
senses.definition: to add salt, herbs, or spice to food
senses.definitionCN: 给食物加盐、香草或香料
senses.example: Season the soup with salt.
senses.why: Bringing food to its right time and condition became flavouring.
senses.whyCN: 让食物达到合适状态引申为调味。

intro.en: Season comes from Latin satio, a sowing, through Old French seison, the time of sowing.
intro.cn: season 源自拉丁语 satio（播种），经古法语 seison（播种时节）进入英语。

items.en: Satio meant a sowing or planting.
items.cn: satio 意为播种或种植。

items.en: Seison meant the time for sowing.
items.cn: seison 意为播种的时节。

items.en: Season meant a suitable time of year.
items.cn: season 意为一年中合适的时节。

items.en: Season came to mean one of the four parts of the year.
items.cn: season 开始指一年四季之一。

items.en: Season also means to flavour food.
items.cn: 现代英语中 season 还表示给食物调味。

note.en: Season is compared with similar-looking words and with words for periods of time.
note.cn: 把 season 与形近词以及表示时间段的词作比较。

entries.definition: a point or period of existence

normalIntro.en: Season is a time of year, and to season is to give food its flavour.
normalIntro.cn: season 是一年中的时节，to season 是给食物调味。

normal.en: There are four seasons in a year.
normal.cn: 一年有四季。

normal.en: In season means available now.
normal.cn: in season 意为当下应季。

normal.en: The rainy season brings floods.
normal.cn: 雨季带来洪水。

normal.en: Seasoning adds flavour to food.
normal.cn: 调味品给食物增添风味。

normal.en: Season and seasoning share a base.
normal.cn: season 与 seasoning 同根。

abstract.en: The word began with the time for sowing.
abstract.cn: 这个词最初指播种的时节。

abstract.en: A time of year and a time for food share one idea of readiness.
abstract.cn: 一年的时节与食物的时机共享「恰当」这一概念。

abstract.en: Seasoning brings food to its best condition.
abstract.cn: 调味让食物达到最佳状态。

examples.en: Winter is the coldest season.
The hotel is busy in season.
Season the soup with salt.

dict_mnemonic.text: season 源自拉丁语 satio（播种），原指播种的时节；一年中的时节后来固定为四季，「调味」义则来自「让食物达到恰当状态」。

root: 源自拉丁语 satio（播种），经古法语 seison（播种时节），核心义「合适的时节」。

sensesIntro.en: Season means one of the four parts of the year, a particular period, or to flavour food.
sensesIntro.cn: season 意为四季之一、某个时期，或给食物调味。

core.en: A fitting time marked by weather or activity.
core.cn: 由天气或活动标记的合适时期。

branches.en: One of the four weather periods.
A time when an activity is common.
The act of flavouring food.
Both are periods marked by what happens then.
branches.cn: 两者都是由当时活动标记的时期。

branches.en: Weather and food both have a right time.
branches.cn: 天气与食物都有合适的时机。

intro.en: Season forms adjectives and nouns for timing and flavour.
intro.cn: season 构成表示时节与风味的形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin satio, sowing, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 satio（播种）是远源。

items.meaning: a time of year, or to flavour

items.example: The four seasons change the land.

items.meaning: salt or spice added to food
the quiet part of the year
a ticket for many events or rides

items.exampleCN: 混合调味料散发着温暖香气。

definition_en: a place to sit, a position in an organization, to place someone in a seat, or to have room for a number of people
core_image: 剧院里一排排红色座椅，灯光亮起，观众陆续入座
scene: 观众在开演前找到自己的座位。The audience found their seats before the show.
sceneCN: 这里 seat 是「座位」（第 1 个义项）；句意：观众在开演前找到自己的座位。

senses.title: A place to sit
senses.definition: a chair or place designed for someone to sit on
senses.definitionCN: 供人坐的椅子或位置
senses.example: Please take a seat.
senses.why: The central sense is the physical place for sitting.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是供人坐的物理位置。

senses.title: A position in a group
senses.definition: a place as a member of a council, parliament, or company
senses.definitionCN: 在议会、委员会或公司中的成员位置
senses.example: She won a seat on the council.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢得了委员会的席位。
senses.why: A physical seat stands for the right to sit and vote.
senses.whyCN: 物理座位代指坐下与投票的权利。

senses.title: To place someone
senses.definition: to place someone in a seat
senses.definitionCN: 安排某人坐下
senses.example: The host seated us by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 主人安排我们坐在窗边。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action of placing someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为安排某人入座的动作。

senses.title: To have room for
senses.definition: to have enough seats for a number of people
senses.definitionCN: 有足够座位容纳一定人数
senses.example: The hall seats five hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳五百人。
senses.why: Counting seats becomes a way of stating capacity.

intro.en: Seat comes from Old Norse sæti, a sitting place, and is related to sit and to Latin sedere.

normal.en: Essay signpost: in argumentative writing, secondly opens the second body paragraph.
normal.cn: 写作路标：议论文里 secondly 常开启第二个主体段落。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder: you have stepped on rung one (firstly) and now lift your foot to rung two — secondly.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子：已踩上第一级（firstly），正抬脚踏上第二级——secondly。

abstract.en: Two checkboxes on a to-do list: the first is ticked, your pen hovers over the second — that hover is secondly.
abstract.cn: 待办清单上两个方框：第一个已打勾，笔尖悬在第二个上方——这一悬停就是 secondly。

abstract.en: A train leaving station one and pulling into station two: each stop of the argument is a numbered platform.
abstract.cn: 列车驶离一站、进站二：论证的每一站都是编了号的月台，secondly 就是第二月台到站声。

examples.en: Firstly, the room is too small; secondly, the rent is too high.
examples.cn: 第一，房间太小；其次，租金太高。

examples.en: Secondly, we must think about how the new rule affects younger students.
examples.cn: 其次，我们必须考虑新规定对低年级学生的影响。

examples.en: She listed two reasons: secondly, the bus would be faster than walking.
examples.cn: 她列了两条理由：其次，坐公交比走路快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞看得了」——第一点已经看完了，塞进脑子里看第二点，看得了第二点就轮到 secondly。

root: 拉丁语 secundus（依次的、跟随其后的）← 动词 sequi（跟随）；经古法语 second 进入中古英语；现代英语加副词后缀 -ly 构成列举路标词。

sensesIntro.en: Two discourse senses: a list signpost, and a carrier for the second supporting argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个话语义项：既是列举路标，也是第二条支持性论据的载体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping to the second mark on an ordered list
core.cn: 核心意象：在有序清单上迈向第二个标记点

branches.en: ENUMERATION: secondly names the second point after first or firstly.
branches.cn: 列举线：secondly 在 first 或 firstly 之后点名第二个要点。

branches.en: ARGUMENT: the second point is stacked to reinforce the case already opened.
branches.cn: 论证线：第二个要点用来强化已经展开的立场。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: it inherits the Latin idea of following what came before.
branches.cn: 顺序线：它继承了拉丁语「跟随在前者之后」的观念。

branches.en: SIGNPOST: the -ly form works like firstly and finally to structure speech.
branches.cn: 路标线：-ly 形式与 firstly、finally 一样为发言搭建结构。

branches.en: FORMALITY: it marks formal, planned discourse rather than casual chat.
branches.cn: 语域线：它标记正式、有准备的语篇，而非随意闲谈。

intro.en: Secondly is a transparent formation: ordinal stem + adverb suffix.
intro.cn: secondly 构词透明：序数词干加副词后缀，一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The ordinal stem traces back to Latin secundus «following».
latinIntro.cn: 序数词干可追溯到拉丁语 secundus「跟随其后的」。

items.meaning: adverb marker: in the second place
items.exampleCN: 第一是成本，其次是安全。

items.meaning: adverb marker: in the first place
forms adverbs from adjectives and nouns
items.meaningCN: 副词后缀，把形容词或名词变为副词
拉丁序数词：依次的、第二的

items.exampleCN: sequor, sequi, secutus（跟随的动词变位）

items.meaningCN: 顺序；序列；同根派生名词

items.meaning: of the second rank; less important

items.meaningCN: 迫害；同根动词，字面「一路跟着纠缠」

definition_zh: 秘密；秘诀；秘密的；保密的
definition_en: something kept hidden from others, a method that works very well, or kept from public knowledge
core_image: 抽屉最里层压着一封没有署名的信，封口已经被摩挲得发白
scene: 她压低声音，把这件事只告诉了最好的朋友。She kept the secret from everyone else.

senses.title: Something hidden

senses.title: A working method

senses.title: Kept from others

normal.en: Keep a secret means not telling others.

normal.en: The secret of success is a hidden working method.

abstract.en: A secret is something set apart from public view.

abstract.en: Keeping a secret is a kind of power and a kind of burden.
abstract.cn: 保守秘密既是一种权力，也是一种负担。

abstract.en: A method becomes a secret when it is not shared.
abstract.cn: 方法不被分享时就成了秘诀。

examples.en: She told me a secret.

examples.cn: 他们举行了一次秘密会议。

items.example: The secret is safe with me.

definition_en: a person who handles letters and records for an organization, an official of a club, or a government minister
core_image: 办公桌一角摞着待签的文件，电话听筒还夹在肩头
scene: 她把会议记录整理好，放到经理桌上。The secretary typed the minutes of the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 secretary 是「秘书」（第 1 个义项）；句意：秘书打出了会议记录。

senses.title: An office assistant
senses.definition: a person employed to handle letters, records, and office tasks
senses.definitionCN: 受雇处理信件、记录与办公事务的人
senses.example: The secretary answered the phone.
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代义。

senses.title: An organization officer
senses.definition: an official who keeps records for a club or organization
senses.definitionCN: 为俱乐部或组织保存记录的负责人
senses.example: She was elected secretary of the club.
senses.why: Clubs use the title for their record keeper.
senses.whyCN: 俱乐部用该头衔称呼记录负责人。

senses.title: A government minister
senses.definition: a senior government official in charge of a department
senses.definitionCN: 负责某个部门的高级政府官员
senses.example: The Foreign Secretary gave a speech.
senses.why: In some governments the title names a minister.
senses.whyCN: 在某些政府中该头衔指部长。

intro.en: Secretary comes from Latin secretarius, an officer trusted with secrets.
intro.cn: secretary 源自拉丁语 secretarius，指受托掌管机密的人员。

items.en: Secretum meant a secret.
items.cn: secretum 意为秘密。

items.en: Secretarius meant a confidential officer.
items.cn: secretarius 意为掌管机密的人员。

items.en: Secretary entered English for a trusted clerk.
items.cn: secretary 以「受信任的文书」之义进入英语。

entries.definition: a person who keeps records or serves customers

normalIntro.en: A secretary keeps records and handles office work, and the title also names club officers and ministers.
normalIntro.cn: secretary 负责记录与办公事务，也可指俱乐部干事与部长。

normal.en: Secretary contains secret, because the job once involved trust.
normal.cn: secretary 含有 secret，因为这个职务曾与信任机密有关。

normal.en: The plural is secretaries, changing y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数是 secretaries，把 y 变成 ies。

normal.en: A secretary general leads an international organization.
normal.cn: secretary general 领导一个国际组织。

normal.en: A press secretary speaks for a government.

normal.en: Secretarial work includes typing and filing.
normal.cn: secretarial work 包括打字与归档。

abstract.en: The keeper of records holds the memory of an office.
abstract.cn: 记录保管者掌握着一个机构的内存。

abstract.en: Trust is the oldest part of the job.

abstract.en: A small title can grow into a government post.

examples.en: The secretary answered the phone.

definition_en: one of the parts into which something is divided, a department, a part of a book, or a cut-away view

senses.title: Area of business

items.en: Today it labels industries and city districts.
items.cn: 如今它用来标记各行业与城区。

note.en: Sector is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts or divisions.
note.cn: 把 sector 与形近词以及表示部分、划分的词作比较。

entries.definition: one of the parts into which something is divided

normalIntro.en: Sector means a cut-out part of a larger whole.
normalIntro.cn: sector 意为从更大整体中切分出来的一块。

normal.en: Sector comes from a Latin verb meaning to cut.
normal.cn: sector 出自一个意为「切」的拉丁语动词。

normal.en: Each slice of a pie chart is a sector.
normal.cn: 饼图中的每一块都是扇形。

normal.en: The service sector sells services, not goods.
normal.cn: 服务业部门卖的是服务而非货物。

normal.en: The public sector is run by the government.
normal.cn: 公共部门由政府运营。

normal.en: Sector and section share the same root.
normal.cn: sector 与 section 同根。

abstract.en: To divide the world into sectors is a way of seeing it.
abstract.cn: 把世界分成部门，是一种观察世界的方式。

abstract.en: From inside, a sector can look like the whole.
abstract.cn: 身处其中时，一个部门可能看起来就是全部。

abstract.en: A sector is always a part of a larger circle.
abstract.cn: 一个扇形始终是更大圆周的一部分。

examples.en: The service sector is growing fast.
She works in the technology sector.
Troops held the northern sector of the city.
examples.cn: 部队控制了城市的北部区域。

dict_mnemonic.text: sector 由拉丁词干 sect（切）加 -or 构成，指「切出来的一块」，引申为部门、扇形与区域。

root: 源自拉丁语 sector（切割者），出自 secare（切），核心义「切分出来的一块」。

sensesIntro.en: Sector means a part of an economy, an area of business, a geometric slice, or a district.
sensesIntro.cn: sector 意为经济部门、行业、扇形或区域。

core.en: A part cut out from a larger whole.
core.cn: 从更大整体中切分出来的一块。

branches.en: A slice of the national economy.
branches.cn: 国民经济中的一个部门。

branches.en: A field of business activity.
A pie-shaped part of a circle.
A district of a city or area.
branches.cn: 城市或区域中划分出的一块。

branches.en: Economic and industry senses overlap.
branches.cn: 经济部门与行业这两个义项相互重叠。

intro.en: Sector belongs to the Latin family of sect, meaning to cut.
intro.cn: sector 属于拉丁词干 sect（切）这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin secare, to cut, is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secare（切）是历史词根。

items.example: The farm sector employs fewer people now.
items.exampleCN: 农业部门如今雇用的人更少了。

items.example: Read the first section of the report.
The sofa is a sectional design.
items.exampleCN: 这张沙发是组合式设计。
各部门政策因行业而异。

items.example: The two roads intersect near the river.
Students dissect a frog in class.
